neighbours.label: the noun ' subject' (also ' topic', ' site') naming what something is about or where it happened, as in 'the subject of'
fire: The missing painting has become the subject of a police investigation.
Her childhood in Lagos is the subject of his latest novel.
Housing costs were the main topic of debate at the town meeting.
The old mine was the subject of a long court case in the 1990s.
His strange disappearance remains the subject of much speculation.
The bridge collapse became a topic of national concern overnight.
The new drug is the subject of three clinical trials in Europe.
The valley is the site of an important Roman settlement.
quiet: The missing painting has led to a police investigation and two arrests.
Her childhood in Lagos is described at length in his latest novel.
Housing costs were debated for hours at the town meeting.
The old mine was fought over in a long court case in the 1990s.
His strange disappearance still causes much speculation.
The bridge collapse caused national concern overnight.
The new drug is being tested in three clinical trials in Europe.
The valley holds the ruins of an important Roman settlement.

notes: Probe: 'the subject of' 0.86-0.96, 'the site of' 0.69, 'the topic of' 0.57; other senses of ' subject' are weaker ('subject to change' 0.22, grammatical subject 0.23, school subject 0.34); paraphrases without the noun <=0.03. Quiet items drop the noun and keep the meaning, so this tests the word rather than the topic.
